title: Routine, comprehensive single-cell proteoform reading

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a practical way to identify and quantify the different intact protein forms present in an individual cell. A proteoform is a particular molecular version of a protein, including its sequence differences and modifications. Reading these forms would establish which modifications occur together on the same molecule, rather than merely detecting a protein family or separate modified fragments.

Synthesis of the intended capability: “comprehensive” means broad, explicitly measured coverage across protein forms and abundances, with disclosed blind spots. “Routine” adds reproducibility, reliable quantification, practical throughput and accessible cost. The concept does not require a particular instrument: nanopore reading and mass spectrometry contribute relevant capabilities, but neither supplied demonstration establishes the complete single-cell measurement system.

significance.text: If achieved, this capability would expose biochemical diversity that DNA sequences and RNA measurements cannot fully specify. Sequence variation and modifications combine on individual protein molecules; measuring those combinations would show which molecular forms coexist within a sampled cell. Its revolutionary contribution would be to make that molecular diversity directly measurable at single-cell resolution.

Conditional synthesis: broad and reliable measurements could help distinguish cellular states that appear similar in gene or RNA measurements, reveal associations between modification combinations and biological behavior, and supply richer evidence for biochemical models. Disease classification and treatment are downstream possibilities requiring separate biological and clinical validation. A proteoform inventory alone would not establish molecular function, causal interactions, spatial organization or the sequence of events that produced the observed state.

The analogy to sequencing is useful insofar as it describes systematic molecular reading, but the demonstrated ability to reread selected protein strands should not be equated with a general protein equivalent of routine DNA sequencing. Full-length protein analysis still faces sensitivity, dynamic-range, throughput and cost limitations, and the nanopore study explicitly identifies de novo amino-acid calling as a further challenge.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is broad identification and quantification of intact proteoforms from complex individual cells while preserving the connection between sequence and modifications on each molecule. Detecting selected modifications or identifying proteins from digested peptides supplies only part of that information. The engineering challenge is to combine sensitivity, abundance range, full-length information, modification assignment and useful coverage within a practical workflow.

For nanopore approaches, distinguishing selected substitutions in known sequence contexts does not solve general de novo reading. The supplied study identifies the need for extensive training datasets for amino-acid callers. Moving from engineered substrates to complex cellular material would also require demonstrated discrimination among diverse sequences and modification combinations, rather than assuming that performance on a defined substrate transfers automatically.

Throughput and coverage remain coupled constraints. Wang and colleagues describe faster single-cell analysis as potentially reducing proteome coverage. Increasing the number of peptide-digest samples analyzed per day therefore does not by itself solve intact-proteoform identification or modification linkage. A successful system would have to demonstrate its breadth and reliability at the speed and cost claimed for routine use.

current_state.text: On 11 September 2024, Motone and colleagues published repeated nanopore reading of engineered long protein strands. The experiments demonstrated discrimination of selected amino-acid substitutions in defined sequence contexts and mapping of selected modifications, including kinase-associated modifications and putative proteoforms of a single synthetic substrate. These results establish useful single-molecule reading capabilities, but not general de novo sequencing of intact proteoforms from a complex cell.

The distinction between experimental results and projections matters within that study. Improvements in rereading classification accuracy were simulated; they were not a demonstration of general sequencing accuracy across cellular proteins. The authors describe direct determination of amino-acid sequences from nanopore signals as a more difficult future task requiring extensive training data.

On 24 September 2026, Wang and colleagues reported a multicolumn NanoLC workflow for high-throughput, label-free single-cell proteomics. The abstract reports approximately 5,000 proteins per 250-pg digest injection, an average of approximately 4,000 per single HeLa cell and maxima exceeding 5,100. The detailed analysis counts protein groups inferred from peptide digests. These numbers therefore describe protein-group identification depth, rather than numbers of intact proteoforms read with their modifications linked.

The HeLa results also require their filtering and timing context. The analysis excluded 169 of 1,230 cell runs, approximately 14%, using an interquartile-range filter, so the reported identification depth should be understood as applying to retained runs rather than as an unfiltered guarantee for every cell. The reported upper throughput of 288 samples per day is nominal: the implemented acquisition included approximately 20–21 seconds of overhead beyond each five-minute cycle. These qualifications constrain interpretation without negating the reported progress.

The supplied review assessed retained article text for both studies. Although the source index also lists saved PDFs and supplementary files, the review did not inspect figure images, raw data or linked external datasets; its conclusions are consequently an assessment of the reported evidence, not an independent reanalysis. Neither supplied study demonstrates the complete proposed capability. The supplied search record does not establish whether other work had closed the remaining gap by 1 November 2026, so the dated findings cannot support an exhaustive claim about the whole field.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: independent laboratories should blind-test complex single cells alongside standards spanning rare and abundant proteins, sequence variants and defined modification combinations. The system should identify and quantify intact proteoforms and demonstrate that modifications assigned to one proteoform occur on the same molecule. Success on selected engineered strands or peptide-digest protein groups would remain a precursor unless this broader capability is also shown.
completion_criteria.label: Independent blind tests quantify single-cell proteoforms with same-molecule modification assignments

completion_criteria.text: Proposed evaluation protocol: define coverage targets, abundance range, acceptable identification and modification-localization errors, quantitative accuracy, missingness, cost and throughput before testing. Report performance by protein and modification class, disclose failed or excluded cell runs, and measure sustained throughput including acquisition overhead. Independent replication should test whether performance survives changes in laboratory, sample preparation and cellular context.
completion_criteria.label: Prespecified performance metrics are reported and independently replicated across contexts

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundary: convincing completion would combine broad molecular coverage with reproducible operation at a cost and speed suitable for large studies. Claims should remain bounded by the tested cell types, protein classes, modification types and abundance ranges. Finite validation can establish demonstrated breadth and useful limits; it cannot prove literal coverage of every possible proteoform.
completion_criteria.label: Broad proteoform coverage is reproducible at large-study cost and speed

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: BCH-02, “Predict biochemical function from molecular sequence and environment,” and BCH-10, “Predict modification-dependent biochemical networks,” could use proteoform measurements as inputs and validation evidence. BCH-05 concerns observing which molecular forms are present; BCH-02 concerns predicting what molecules do, while BCH-10 concerns predicting interactions and network behavior as modifications change. Measurement alone does not supply either predictive capability.

Roster-based synthesis: BCH-06, “A multiplexed biochemical flight recorder for living cells,” concerns recording biochemical history. BCH-05 would characterize the proteoforms present at sampling. A recorded history might explain how that state arose, but a detailed inventory does not by itself reconstruct prior events or their order.

Roster-based synthesis: BCH-11, “Routine structural reading of complex glycans,” shares the goal of making heterogeneous biochemical structures routinely readable. Glycan-bearing proteins create a potential overlap, but intact-proteoform identification does not automatically resolve complex glycan structure, and glycan structural reading does not automatically establish the full sequence and modification combination of its carrier protein.

Roster-based synthesis: BCH-01, “General design of enzymes for new chemical reactions,” BCH-08, “Resolve the nitrogenase reaction cycle during nitrogen fixation,” and BCH-09, “Predict and control the biochemical organization of condensates,” could benefit from knowing the protein forms present in an experiment. Their central goals remain distinct: designing catalytic activity, resolving a reaction mechanism, and predicting or controlling molecular organization. Proteoform inventories would provide evidence rather than establish those outcomes.

Roster-based synthesis: BCH-03, “A self-maintaining, evolvable cell assembled from defined components,” could use comprehensive proteoform measurements to characterize an assembled cell, but characterization would not demonstrate self-maintenance or evolution. BCH-04, “A chemically plausible route from simple feedstocks to evolving heredity,” and BCH-07, “Autonomous heredity in a chemically distinct genetic polymer,” concern the origin or implementation of heredity. Protein measurement could support experiments in those areas without establishing their central breakthroughs.

change_log.change: Preserved BCH-05 and its title while explaining intact proteoforms, linked modifications and the practical meaning of routine coverage.
change_log.reason: The concept remains a coherent measurement innovation despite limitations in individual supporting assertions.

change_log.change: Removed the unqualified assertion that proteins cannot generally be amplified like DNA and retained the documented analytical barriers.
change_log.reason: The supplied review did not establish the amplification assertion; its evidentiary gap does not contradict or invalidate the broader concept.

change_log.change: Expanded the nanopore account to identify engineered substrates, defined sequence contexts, selected modification mapping and simulated accuracy improvements.
change_log.reason: These distinctions preserve the experimental achievement while preventing it from being presented as general de novo cellular proteoform sequencing.

change_log.change: Corrected the single-cell identification account to protein groups from digests and added the 250-pg result, reported maxima, excluded runs and acquisition overhead.
change_log.reason: Identification depth and throughput require their counting, filtering and timing context; none measures comprehensive intact-proteoform reading.

change_log.change: Separated direct measurement benefits from conditional biological and clinical applications.
change_log.reason: Observing molecular diversity does not automatically establish function, causation, disease classification or treatment benefit.

change_log.change: Developed completion criteria as explicit proposals with predefined metrics, independent replication and bounded coverage claims.
change_log.reason: The supplied papers motivate evaluation dimensions but do not establish a universal acceptance standard.

change_log.change: Preserved the review's limits on inspected material and field-wide freshness, and distinguished every other roster entry through labeled synthesis.
change_log.reason: Saved artifacts do not imply independent inspection, two dated studies do not establish an exhaustive field assessment, and conceptual overlap does not justify merging innovations.

unresolved_issues: The supplied evidence does not establish the protein-amplification assertion; it remains omitted rather than treated as disproven.
Field-wide openness as of 1 November 2026 remains unverified because the supplied freshness search record is empty.
Coverage targets, acceptable errors, abundance range, cost and sustained throughput for a convincing routine system remain to be defined.
Generalization from engineered nanopore substrates to diverse cellular proteins and modification combinations remains undemonstrated in the supplied evidence.
The review did not independently inspect figure images, raw data or linked external datasets, leaving those aspects outside this record's evidentiary assessment.

brief.title: Reading the full variety of proteins in one cell
possible: Researchers could identify and measure the different whole protein forms inside a single cell. Each form, called a proteoform, combines a protein’s sequence with its chemical modifications. Reading whole molecules would reveal which modifications occur together on the same protein.
A practical system would let researchers compare these protein forms across large studies, including both rare and abundant forms, with reliable measurements and clear limits on what it can detect.
why: Cells that look alike in their DNA or RNA measurements can contain different protein forms. Measuring those differences could help researchers distinguish cell states and connect combinations of protein modifications with biological behavior.
Biochemical models could draw on measurements of the protein forms that actually coexist inside a cell. DNA sequences and RNA measurements cannot fully specify that diversity.

sources.showed: They repeatedly read engineered protein strands through a nanopore, a tiny sensing hole. They distinguished selected changes in protein building blocks and mapped selected chemical modifications.
sources.quote:
we demonstrate the ability to reread individual 
protein molecules multiple times
sources.cited_for: Individual protein molecules can be reread, with sensitivity to selected sequence differences and modifications.
sources.not_established: The work does not establish general reading of unknown protein sequences or broad measurement of intact protein forms from a cell.

sources.showed: They built a system that rapidly separates protein fragments for identification and measurement. It maintained stable operation across extended runs and analyzed individual cells.
sources.quote: The system provides stable peptide separation, negligible carryover, and robust retention-time reproducibility across nearly 1200 consecutive injections.
sources.cited_for: Fast, sustained analysis of protein fragments can support large studies of individual cells.
sources.not_established: Identifying protein groups from fragments does not reveal intact proteoforms or which modifications share a molecule.

shown: Motone and colleagues demonstrated selected features of whole engineered protein strands. Wang and colleagues reported an average of about 4,000 protein groups per retained HeLa cell, inferred from fragments after filtering out some cell runs. These are separate advances toward molecular detail and practical scale.
missing: Broad identification and measurement of intact proteoforms in individual cells, with modifications linked to the molecules carrying them, remains to be shown.
General reading of unknown protein sequences and diverse modification combinations remains to be demonstrated beyond engineered strands.
A complete system still needs to combine broad coverage, reliable measurements, practical speed and affordable cost.

milestones.label: Blind tests measure whole protein forms in individual cells
milestones.explanation: Independent laboratories would have to measure intact proteoforms in blind tests of complex cells and standards, linking modifications on each molecule. This would establish the central capability.

milestones.label: Independent replication meets performance targets across conditions
milestones.explanation: Tests would have to meet predefined targets for coverage, errors, measurement accuracy, missing results, cost and sustained speed across laboratories and cell contexts. This would establish reliability beyond a single setup.

milestones.label: Broad coverage works reliably at large-study cost and speed
milestones.explanation: A system would have to reproduce broad proteoform coverage at a cost and speed suitable for large studies, within clearly tested limits. This would make the capability practical for routine research.

uncertain: The coverage, error rates, abundance range, cost and sustained speed needed to count as routine remain to be defined.
Performance on engineered proteins may not transfer to the diversity of sequences and modification combinations inside cells.
Finite tests can establish useful breadth and blind spots, but cannot prove coverage of every possible proteoform.

page.title: Single-cell proteoform identification and quantification
page.definition: Individual human cells yield inventories of intact proteoforms, the molecular versions of proteins defined by sequence and chemical modifications. Each form present at 10 copies per cell or more is identified with its complete sequence and linked modifications and is quantified.

goal.need: NHGRI estimates that about 10,000 human genes produce proteins above 20 copies per cell in a typical cell type, while intracellular protein abundances span 7–10 orders of magnitude. Gene-level identification does not specify which sequence variants and chemical modifications coexist on each protein molecule. Proteoform analysis supplies that molecular composition.

statements.quote: generate a definitive set of reference proteoforms produced from the genome
statements.context: The Human Proteoform Project proposes a reference atlas; its cell-based approach can initially use thousands of cells of each type.

statements.quote: protein sequencing data at sufficient scale, speed, cost and accuracy to use routinely
statements.context: This passage describes the long-term objective of the single-molecule protein sequencing programme.

completion.title: Independent laboratories recover complete single-cell proteoform inventories above a 10-copy floor.
completion.criterion: An originating laboratory and an independent laboratory each identify and relatively quantify every intact proteoform present at 10 copies per cell or more in individual human cells of a specified cell type. Each identification resolves the complete amino-acid sequence, gene of origin, and identities and positions of all modifications, satisfying CTDP Level 1. Completeness and quantitative recovery are validated against orthogonal reference measurements, including recovery controls at the 10-copy floor. This is an Atlas adaptation of a cell-type target.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback, combining Kelleher's proposed cell-type coverage target with CTDP Level 1 identification and independent reproduction.
completion.basis: NHGRI/NCI funding calls, Human Proteoform Project proposals and CTDP identification criteria were searched; no combined single-cell completion test was found. Kelleher proposed “100 % sequence coverage for proteoforms detected at a copy number of 10 and above.” That target concerns cell types sampled in bulk. Applying it to individual cells, requiring quantitative recovery and adding independent reproduction are Atlas extensions.

milestones.title: An intact proteoform is identified without sequence or modification ambiguity.
milestones.criterion: Identify an intact proteoform with its complete amino-acid sequence, gene of origin, and identities and locations of every post-translational modification resolved: CTDP Level 1. This classification specifies structural ambiguity, not statistical confidence. On 11 September 2024, Motone and colleagues demonstrated substitution discrimination and phosphorylation mapping on engineered strands; those selected readouts do not establish complete Level 1 identification of unknown cellular proteoforms.
milestones.set_by: Consortium for Top-Down Proteomics, five-level proteoform identification classification published in Nature Methods in 2019.
milestones.threshold_quote: The proteoform is identified with no ambiguity

milestones.title: A single-cell assay quantifies at least 1,000 unique proteins and detects proteoforms and modifications.
milestones.criterion: Identify and quantify at least 1,000 unique proteins per cell simultaneously and detect proteoforms and post-translational modifications, with utility for cancer research or clinical translation. This is NCI's technology funding criterion. On 24 September 2026, Wang and colleagues reported a median of 4,038 peptide-inferred protein groups in 1,061 retained HeLa-cell runs; 169 of 1,230 runs were excluded. Protein-group depth alone does not establish the proteoform and modification requirements.
milestones.set_by: National Cancer Institute, technology eligibility criterion in Section I of RFA-HG-21-001, published on 9 July 2021.
milestones.threshold_quote: identify and quantify at least 1000 unique proteins per cell at once and also detect proteoforms and PTMs

milestones.title: One laboratory recovers a complete single-cell proteoform inventory above 10 copies per form.
milestones.criterion: In one laboratory, identify and relatively quantify every intact proteoform present at 10 copies per cell or more in individual human cells of a specified type, with complete sequence coverage, modification linkage and Level 1 identification. Validate completeness and quantitative recovery against orthogonal measurements and recovery controls. On 14 July 2026, Kanchustambham and colleagues reported about 400 proteoforms across more than 17,000 keratinocyte nuclei, using intact-mass matching to a bulk reference library; this does not establish complete inventories of individual whole cells.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback: searches of NHGRI/NCI calls, Human Proteoform Project proposals and CTDP criteria found no published integrated single-cell prototype gate. The 10-copy target was proposed for bulk cell-type analysis.

not_found: No external completion test combining comprehensive intact-proteoform coverage, single-cell quantification and independent reproduction was found.
No published acceptance limits defining routine single-cell proteoform analysis by quantitative error, sustained throughput or per-cell cost were found.
The full texts of the 2014 CTDP pilot study and 2023 single-cell benchmarking recommendations could not be opened beyond access checks.

results.finding: One synthetic protein substrate: more than 100 putative proteoforms were relatively quantified; the number of reads is not stated.
results.detail: Phosphorylation states were inferred by matching signals to models of a designed substrate. The study did not resolve the complete sequence and all modifications of an unknown proteoform at CTDP Level 1.
results.quote:
Moreover, we applied our method to detect and map the activities of 
distinct kinases, achieving site-specific detection of enzymatic PTMs 
along extended protein sequences and the relative quantification of 
more than 100 putative proteoforms of a single synthetic protein sub-
strate.

results.finding: Among 1,061 retained single HeLa-cell runs, the median was 4,038 identified protein groups.
results.detail: Of 1,230 single-cell runs, 169 were excluded. Proteins were inferred from digested peptides; the study does not establish detection of intact proteoforms and their modifications.
results.quote: The box plots show the median protein identifications (25th–75th percentiles) were 5079 (5019–5138.75) for 250 pg HeLa digest QC and 4038 (3686.5–4309.5) for single HeLa cells.

results.finding: In lysate from 45 million Jurkat cells, top-down analysis identified 3,603 Level 1 proteoforms.
results.detail: Level 1 denotes no reported ambiguity in sequence, gene of origin, PTM identity or PTM localization. The classification depends on the search parameters and database; the search included modified residues annotated in UniProt.
results.quote: There were 3603 unambiguous level 1 proteoform identifications, consisting of 206 unique protein accessions.

results.finding: In 200 normal and cholangiocarcinoma cells, an average of 2,548 proteins per cell were identified.
results.detail: The assay detected variant and post-translationally modified peptides and showed cancer-research utility. The reported per-cell average is for identified proteins; the text does not establish that at least 1,000 proteins were quantified in each cell.
results.quote:
A total of 4197 proteins (41,560 peptides) were
identiﬁed from 200 single cells with an average of 2548 proteins per single
cell (Fig. 1d, Fig. S4a and Supplementary Data 1).

results.finding: Four single HeLa cells were analyzed; up to 64 proteoforms were identified in one cell using match-between-runs.
results.detail: Proteoform abundances were compared across cells, but the study does not establish complete inventories above 10 copies per form, complete sequence coverage, Level 1 identification, or validated quantitative recovery.
results.quote: The number of identifications could be improved by employing an MBR strategy to reach 48 protein and 64 proteoform identifications from a single HeLa cell.
